Naïve is a San Francisco technology research organization founded in 2025 by Sean Dorje and Dennis Zax. The company develops infrastructure designed to let artificial intelligence agent teams operate entire business workflows end to end. Instead of operating as conversational chat interfaces, agents deployed through the platform operate with dedicated digital credentials, email addresses, and computational resources. The system provides pre-configured templates that coordinate specialized teams across content creation, search optimization, client outreach, and media production. The organization participated in the Spring 2025 batch of Y Combinator.

In one minute

- ·Provides runtime infrastructure for artificial intelligence agent teams to operate full business functions.
- ·Equips autonomous agents with independent operational credentials, accounts, and execution environments.
- ·Supplies pre-built workflow templates across media generation, digital marketing, and client communications.
- ·Founded by Sean Dorje and Dennis Zax, backed by Y Combinator in the Spring 2025 cohort.

Our take

## Our take

Building commercial artificial intelligence applications often fragments across disjointed tooling for messaging, payment processing, and document filing. Naïve proposes a unified runtime where autonomous agent teams take on operational responsibilities with dedicated computational and financial identities. Allowing software systems to orchestrate marketing outreach and content creation continuously establishes a novel operating framework. Tracking whether business owners achieve positive operating margins using autonomous worker setups will demonstrate viability.

Tracking client acquisition metrics and ongoing operational costs for businesses operated by autonomous agent teams will prove the model.

The space

## What problem Naïve works on

Many businesses run on repeatable processes across media, marketing, and client services. Coordinating those processes often means stitching together many tools and people, which can be complex and costly. AI agents promise to take on that coordination, but making them work reliably end to end is hard. It requires clear instructions, safe boundaries, and ways to handle exceptions. Naïve addresses this by offering a runtime where agent teams are declared in a config file and run as a unit. This approach aims to make autonomous operations easier to deploy and manage.

In more detail

## What Naïve does, and for whom

Naïve develops an autonomous business runtime where artificial intelligence agent teams operate commercial workflows, digital marketing channels, and client outreach.

**Who uses it.** Digital entrepreneurs, marketing agency operators, and venture studios building automated online business operations.

How it works

- •Business operators define organizational goals or connect their existing digital software tool stack.
- •The runtime initializes autonomous agents equipped with required communication and computation permissions.
- •Agent teams execute operational tasks continuously, recording outcomes and updating business strategies.

## Who else works on this

### Artisan

[artisan.co→](https://www.artisan.co/)

Artisan builds artificial intelligence workers designed to automate business-to-business sales prospecting and outreach campaigns.

**How it differs.** Artisan focuses specifically on outbound sales development and lead discovery, whereas Naïve provides infrastructure for orchestrating multi-discipline autonomous teams across diverse business operations.

### Relevance AI

[relevanceai.com→](https://relevanceai.com/)

Relevance AI offers a platform for enterprise organizations to create and coordinate specialized artificial intelligence workforces.

**How it differs.** Relevance AI emphasizes internal workflow automation for corporate departments, whereas Naïve equips agents with independent operational credentials to run public-facing commercial enterprises.

### CrewAI

[crewai.com→](https://www.crewai.com/)

CrewAI delivers an orchestration runtime for building and managing collaborative artificial intelligence agent multi-agent systems.

**How it differs.** CrewAI provides developer frameworks for building multi-agent software scripts, whereas Naïve provides complete autonomous company templates with dedicated credentials and cloud execution resources.
